article_title: Self-reported patient safety competence among Canadian medical students and postgraduate trainees: a cross-sectional survey.
citation: Doyle Patricia, VanDenKerkhof Elizabeth G, Edge Dana S, Ginsburg Liane, Goldstein David H. (2015). Self-reported patient safety competence among Canadian medical students and postgraduate trainees: a cross-sectional survey. BMJ Quality & Safety. https://doi.org/10.1136/bmjqs-2014-003142
title: Reduced H-PEPSS: 16-item survey measuring six sociocultural patient safety competencies plus clinical skills, classroom and clinical settings
description: The reduced Health Professional Education in Patient Safety Survey (H-PEPSS) is a validated questionnaire measuring learners' confidence in learning six sociocultural patient safety competencies based on the Canadian Patient Safety Institute's Safety Competencies Framework, plus a clinical skills dimension of four items. Respondents answer each item separately for classroom and clinical settings on a 5-point Likert scale; the modified stem reads 'I feel confident in what I am learning about…'. Confirmatory factor analysis in both samples achieved good fit (CFI >0.95, RMSEA <0.06).
requirements: The modified present-tense stem was not validated with students, so the authors revalidated the factor structure with confirmatory factor analysis before interpreting scores
target_learning_goals: self-reported confidence in patient safety learning across six sociocultural competencies and clinical skills
examples: Administered web-based in January 2012 to 255 medical students and 141 postgraduate trainees, taking approximately 12 min to complete
